title_en: Jinan Municipal People's Procuratorate v. Wang Huaizhong — bribery and possession of property from unidentified sources

full_text_en:
Jinan Municipal People's Procuratorate

v.

Wang Huaizhong — Dispute over Bribery and Holding a Huge Amount of Property with Unidentified Sources

(This case was deliberated and decided by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court at its 1308th session)

[Ruling Summary]

The amount of bribes accepted by the defendant was especially huge, and he had the statutory aggravating circumstance of repeatedly demanding bribes. Moreover, in order to evade legal sanctions, during the period when the relevant authorities were investigating his suspected economic crimes, he continued to demand bribes from others and used the huge amount of bribes he demanded in an attempt to prevent the relevant authorities from investigating his economic crimes. The circumstances of the bribery crime were especially egregious, the harm to society was extremely great, and the crime was extremely serious.

Criminal Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2004) Xing Fu Zi No. 15

Defendant Wang Huaizhong, male, born on August 1, 1946, in Bozhou City, Anhui Province, Han ethnicity, university education, formerly Deputy Governor of the Anhui Provincial People's Government and a deputy to the Ninth Anhui Provincial People's Congress (deputy status revoked on September 28, 2002), formerly served as Deputy Secretary of the Fuyang Prefectural Committee of the CPC, Commissioner of the Fuyang Prefectural Administrative Office, Secretary of the Fuyang Prefectural Committee of the CPC, and Secretary of the Fuyang Municipal Committee of the CPC. Resides at Room 102, Building 3, No. 2 Shucheng Road, Hefei City, Anhui Province. Arrested on October 14, 2002. Currently in custody.

The Jinan Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province, after hearing the case filed by the Jinan Municipal People's Procuratorate charging the defendant Wang Huaizhong with the crime of bribery and the crime of holding a huge amount of property with unidentified sources, rendered a criminal judgment (2003) Ji Xing Er Chu Zi No. 32 on December 29, 2003, finding the defendant Wang Huaizhong guilty of the crime of bribery, sentencing him to death, depriving him of political rights for life, and confiscating all his personal property; guilty of the crime of holding a huge amount of property with unidentified sources, sentencing him to four years' imprisonment; and deciding to execute the death penalty, deprive him of political rights for life, and confiscate all his personal property. After the judgment was pronounced, Wang Huaizhong, dissatisfied, filed an appeal. The Shandong High People's Court, by criminal ruling (2004) Lu Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 6 on January 15, 2004, rejected the appeal, affirmed the original judgment, and submitted the case to this Court for approval according to law. This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and conducted a review of the case. The review is now concluded.

The review has found that the judgment of the first instance court determined the following:

In September 1994, the defendant Wang Huaizhong, taking advantage of his position as Deputy Secretary of the Fuyang Prefectural Committee of the CPC and Commissioner of the Fuyang Prefectural Administrative Office, instructed Wang Hanqing and others, including the original Mayor of Fuyang City, to go through the procedures of releasing on bail pending trial for Yang Xiaoming, Deputy Chairman of the Board of Fuyang Feilong Leather Co., Ltd., who was suspected of tax evasion. In December of the same year, Wang Huaizhong accepted RMB 60,000 from Yang Xiaoming.

From 1995 to 1997, the defendant Wang Huaizhong, taking advantage of his positions as Commissioner of the Fuyang Prefectural Administrative Office and Secretary of the Fuyang Municipal Committee of the CPC, repeatedly presided over coordination meetings attended by responsible persons from relevant departments of the Fuyang Prefectural Administrative Office and Fuyang City to resolve issues such as the allocation of construction land for the International Industrial Park and Yinhai Garden projects developed by Anhui Guoyin Fuyang International Industrial Park Development Co., Ltd. in Fuyang City, and to reduce or exempt the urban construction supporting fees for the second phase of the Yinhai Garden project. At the end of July 1997, Wang Huaizhong accepted AUD 10,000 (equivalent to RMB 61,000) from Xiang Kun, Chairman of the Board of the company.

From 1997 to 2000, the defendant Wang Huaizhong, taking advantage of his position as Secretary of the Fuyang Municipal Committee of the CPC, repeatedly presided over coordination meetings attended by responsible persons from relevant departments of Fuyang City to resolve issues such as land use, demolition, and resettlement for the development of the Fuyang Commercial City and Jingshan Villa by Anhui Fuyang Huixin Development Co., Ltd. He accepted RMB 400,000 in total on four separate occasions from Jiang Xu, Yu Yongqiang, and Wang Zhong, responsible persons of the company.

In October 1998, the defendant Wang Huaizhong, taking advantage of his position as Secretary of the Fuyang Municipal Committee of the CPC, requested relevant departments of Fuyang City to resolve the demolition issues encountered by Anhui Fuyang Longteng Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Longteng Company) during the development of Jingxin Villa, and accepted RMB 300,000 from Ma Ping, Chairman of the Board of Longteng Company, and Lu Qiang (Ma Ping's husband), General Manager. In January 1999, Wang Huaizhong, taking advantage of his position as Secretary of the Fuyang Municipal Committee of the CPC, requested the public security organs of Fuyang City not to pursue the liability of Longteng Hotel employees for smashing the glass windows and vehicles of Buckingham Palace Hotel, and afterwards accepted RMB 400,000 from Ma Ping and Lu Qiang. In February of the same year, Wang Huaizhong signed an opinion on Longteng Company's "Report on the Construction of Longteng Shopping Center," requesting support from relevant departments of Fuyang City, and afterwards accepted RMB 200,000 from Ma Ping and Lu Qiang. In May of the same year, Wang Huaizhong spoke to relevant leaders of Yingzhou District, Fuyang City, to help Longteng Company obtain the land use certificate for the Longteng gas station, and accepted RMB 200,000 from Ma Ping and Lu Qiang.

From August 1998 to August 1999, the defendant Wang Huaizhong, taking advantage of his position as Secretary of the Fuyang Municipal Committee of the CPC, signed opinions on seven separate occasions on reports submitted by Zhou Wei, Chairman of the Board of Fuyang Dongfang Hotel, regarding the buyout of Dongfang Hotel and the application for working capital loans, to assist Zhou Wei in buying out Dongfang Hotel and coordinating loans totaling RMB 14.963 million. He accepted RMB 500,000 in total from Zhou Wei on four separate occasions.

In April 1997, the defendant Wang Huaizhong, taking advantage of his position as Secretary of the Fuyang Municipal Committee of the CPC, presided over a coordination meeting attended by responsible persons from relevant departments of Fuyang City, requesting the reduction or exemption of urban construction supporting fees, land transfer fees, and transportation taxes for the development of the Qiyun Building by Anhui Tianli Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. In August 1999, Wang Huaizhong accepted RMB 100,000 from Wang Xinhua, Chairman of the Board of the company.

From the second half of 1996 to January 1999, the defendant Wang Huaizhong, taking advantage of his position as Secretary of the Fuyang Municipal Committee of the CPC, presided over coordination meetings attended by responsible persons from relevant departments of Fuyang City to resolve the demolition issues encountered during the expansion of Buckingham Palace Hotel by Fuyang Buckingham Palace Hotel Co., Ltd., and on two occasions requested the Fuyang Office of Anhui Trust and Investment Company to provide construction funds totaling RMB 3.2 million for Buckingham Palace Hotel. In August 1999, Wang Huaizhong accepted RMB 200,000 from Liu Shiqiang, Chairman of the Board of the company.

From February 1996 to November 1998, the defendant Wang Huaizhong, taking advantage of his position as Secretary of the Fuyang Municipal Committee of the CPC, through means such as convening coordination meetings and approving documents, reduced or exempted fees including land transfer fees and urban construction supporting fees totaling RMB 1.4929 million for Fuyang Luzhou Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., where Ni Chao worked. In May 2000, while attending a meeting in Tianjin, Wang Huaizhong demanded and accepted RMB 50,000 from Ni Chao.

From July 1996 to 1999, the defendant Wang Huaizhong, taking advantage of his position as Secretary of the Fuyang Municipal Committee of the CPC, through means such as approving documents and convening coordination meetings, reduced or exempted fees including urban construction supporting fees and fixed asset investment adjustment taxes totaling RMB 5.87448 million for Anhui Fuyang International Trade Mall Co., Ltd., Anhui Guoli Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., and Anhui Yajie International Trade Group Co., Ltd., where Li Zhou served as the legal representative. In December 2000, Wang Huaizhong, who had been promoted to Deputy Governor of the Anhui Provincial People's Government, upon learning that relevant authorities were investigating his suspected economic crimes, demanded and accepted RMB 2 million from Li Zhou. He gave RMB 1.2 million of this amount to Hou Wanqing (alias "Chen Siyu", who has been sentenced for fraud) as "activity funds" in an attempt to prevent the relevant authorities from investigating his economic crimes, and instructed Yang Yingyu to keep the remaining RMB 800,000.

In December 2000 and February 2001, the defendant Wang Huaizhong, taking advantage of his position as Deputy Governor of the Anhui Provincial People's Government in charge of agricultural work, demanded and accepted RMB 200,000 from Wang Jing, Chairman of the Board of Anhui Niuwang Piye Clothing (Group) Co., Ltd., which planned to establish an agricultural base in Bozhou, Anhui, and demanded and accepted RMB 500,000 from Deng Shuangmei and her husband Yu Dansheng, responsible persons of Anhui Yunpeng Real Estate Co., Ltd., which was preparing to build the Changqing Town Agricultural High-tech Park project. He instructed Yu Dansheng to give RMB 300,000 of this amount to Yu Yongqiang, Deputy Manager of Beijing New Century Sihuan Investment Co., Ltd., and RMB 200,000 to individual business operator Su Huiman, to be used for seeking connections in an attempt to prevent the relevant authorities from investigating his suspected economic crimes.

After the case was initiated, the investigative authorities lawfully seized and froze the property of the defendant Wang Huaizhong. Apart from the proceeds from the bribery crime and his lawful income, Wang Huaizhong could not explain the lawful source of property valued at RMB 4,805,811.03.

The above facts are confirmed by witness testimony, documentary evidence, expert conclusions, and other evidence that was cross-examined at the first instance trial, which is true and sufficient, and the first instance court confirmed them, thereby rendering the first instance judgment.

The defendant Wang Huaizhong, dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, appealed, arguing: The facts determined in the first instance judgment were basically true, but after demanding and accepting RMB 2 million from Li Zhou, he instructed Yang Yingyu to return RMB 800,000 of that amount to Li Zhou; therefore, the amount of the bribe on this occasion should be RMB 1.2 million. The sentence of the first instance judgment was too heavy. After the first instance judgment was pronounced, he reported the crimes of others, showing genuine repentance, and requested a lighter punishment. The defense counsel for Wang Huaizhong, in addition to presenting the same defense arguments as Wang Huaizhong, further argued: The circumstances of Wang Huaizhong's bribery crime had not reached an especially serious degree; the sentence for the bribery crime in the first instance judgment was too heavy, and a lighter punishment was recommended. The method for calculating the property with unidentified sources was incorrect, and there was a possibility of double counting.

The Shandong High People's Court, upon review in the second instance, confirmed that Wang Huaizhong's reasons for defense and the opinions of his defense counsel were all untenable, and therefore rendered a ruling affirming the first instance judgment, rejecting his appeal, and submitted the case to this Court for approval according to law.

This Court, upon review, finds that the defendant Wang Huaizhong, as a state functionary, took advantage of his position to demand and accept RMB 2.75 million, illegally accepted RMB 2.3 million and AUD 10,000, totaling the equivalent of RMB 5.171 million, and sought benefits for relevant entities and individuals. His conduct constituted the crime of bribery. Wang Huaizhong's property and expenditures clearly exceeded his lawful income by a huge margin, and he could not explain the lawful source of property valued at RMB 4,805,811.03. His conduct constituted the crime of holding a huge amount of property with unidentified sources. The amount of bribes accepted by Wang Huaizhong was especially huge, and he had the statutory aggravating circumstance of repeatedly demanding bribes. What is even more egregious is that, in order to evade legal sanctions, during the period when the relevant authorities were investigating his suspected economic crimes, he continued to demand bribes from others, and used the huge amount of bribes he demanded in an attempt to prevent the relevant authorities from investigating his economic crimes. The circumstances of the bribery crime were especially egregious, the harm to society was extremely great, and the crime was extremely serious. During the trial, Wang Huaizhong reported the crimes of others, but upon investigation by the relevant authorities, his reports either lacked specific details such as time and place and did not meet the conditions for filing a case for investigation, or the persons involved had already been reported and investigated prior to Wang Huaizhong's report, or the conduct did not constitute a crime. Wang Huaizhong's conduct did not meet the requirements for meritorious service set forth in Article 68, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, and he had no statutory circumstance for a lighter punishment. During the first instance trial, Wang Huaizhong refused to admit guilt. During the second instance trial, Wang Huaizhong confessed to most of his crimes, but still denied other criminal facts supported by conclusive evidence, which was insufficient to warrant a lighter punishment. The facts found in the first instance judgment and the second instance ruling are clear, the evidence is true and sufficient, the convictions are accurate, the sentences are appropriate, and the trial procedures are lawful. Pursuant to Article 199 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 285, item (1) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ruled as follows:

Approve the criminal ruling of the Shandong High People's Court (2004) Lu Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 6, which affirmed the first instance judgment sentencing the defendant Wang Huaizhong to death for the crime of bribery, depriving him of political rights for life, and confiscating all his personal property; sentencing him to four years' imprisonment for the crime of holding a huge amount of property with unidentified sources; and deciding to execute the death penalty, deprive him of political rights for life, and confiscate all his personal property.

This ruling shall take legal effect upon service.

Presiding Judge: Ren Weihua

Judge: Han Weizhong

Acting Judge: Guo Qingguo

February 11, 2004

Court Clerk: Cui Ran

[Introduction to the Presiding Judge]

Ren Weihua, Senior Judge: Born in 1953, holds a bachelor's degree in law. Appointed Deputy Chief Judge of the First Criminal Adjudication Division of the Supreme People's Court in 1998, and Deputy Chief Judge of the Second Criminal Adjudication Division of the Supreme People's Court from 2000.
